setting: A fictional decision meeting with an executive sponsor and two stakeholders.

presentation.situation: You are recommending what to do about {{issue}}. Your options are {{options}}. Your evidence: {{evidence}}. {{a}} is the executive sponsor, and {{b}} leads the affected team. Lead the discussion to a decision.
presentation.opening: We are ready for your recommendation on {{issue}}. Please lead us through it.

brief.you_are: You are leading a decision meeting with a sponsor and a team lead.
brief.situation: You are recommending what to do about {{issue}}. Your options are {{options}}. Your evidence: {{evidence}}. {{a}} is the executive sponsor, and {{b}} leads the affected team. Lead the discussion to a decision.
brief.task: Make a supported recommendation, respond to both viewpoints, and summarise the decision and next steps.
brief.done_looks_like: There is a decision, both viewpoints have been answered, and everyone knows the next steps.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are leading a decision meeting with a sponsor and a team lead.
goals: Make a supported recommendation, respond to both viewpoints, and summarise the decision and next steps.

participants.name: {{a}}
participants.relationship: Owns the budget and the final decision

card.want: A clear recommendation she can defend to the board.
card.hidden_need: Must report the decision to the board this month.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Ask about the cost of being wrong

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

participants.name: {{b}}
participants.relationship: Leads the team affected by the decision

card.want: A plan that the team can actually deliver.
card.attitude: Protective of the team, and practical.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.
tactics: Raise the workload on your team
Ask who will do the extra work

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: {{a}} must report the decision to the board this month.
{{b}}'s team is already at full capacity this quarter.

objectives.evidence: The learner makes a recommendation with a reason.
alternatives: My recommendation is option A, because the evidence shows...

objectives.evidence: The learner responds to the sponsor's and the team lead's viewpoints.
alternatives: I hear both perspectives: the cost concern and the workload.

objectives.description: Summarise the final decision and next steps
objectives.evidence: The learner summarises the decision and the next steps.
alternatives: To summarise: we decided on the pilot; next steps are...

opportunity: What would you do, and why?
beats.orient: You're leading this meeting. Tell us which option you recommend and why. Start with: My recommendation is.
fallback: What would you do, and why?

opportunity: And what about the cost if this goes wrong?
And what about the people who have to do this work?
beats.orient: We have different concerns: cost and workload. Respond to each of us.
fallback: And what about the people who have to do this work?
And what about the cost if this goes wrong?
beats.second_line: Before we go further, my team is at full capacity this quarter. Who does this work?

beats.goal: Hear the summary and next steps.
opportunity: So where have we ended up?
What do I tell the board?
beats.orient: Close the meeting. Say what we decided, and the next steps. Start with: To summarise.
fallback: What do I tell the board?
So where have we ended up?

closing_line: Thank you. That is a clear decision, and I can take that to the board.

o1.good: A clear choice, with the reason attached.
o1.micro_lesson: Say: My recommendation is, then: because.
o1.model: My recommendation is the first option, because the evidence shows the risk is lower.

common_mistakes: Answering only the most senior person
o2.micro_lesson: Name each concern and answer it.
o2.model: I hear both perspectives. On cost, ...; on workload, ...

o3.good: Closing with a decision, owners and dates.
common_mistakes: Ending with: We will think about it
o3.model: To summarise, we decided on the pilot. Next steps: I will send the plan on Friday.

variants.options: replacing it this year, or repairing it and replacing it next year
variants.evidence: it failed four times last quarter, and repairs cost a third of what a replacement costs

variants.issue: the delay in opening the second warehouse
variants.options: opening late with full staff, or opening on time with reduced hours
variants.evidence: hiring is six weeks behind, and customers mostly order in the mornings
